newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia could stop sale of Gazprom shares on RTS.
newsitem.headline: Russia could stop sale of Gazprom shares on RTS.

text.p: Trading of shares in natural gas producer Gazprom could stop after July 1 on Russia's main equities market if it is not included by then on a list of approved trading floors, the exchange said on Monday.

"Yes, I don't rule out that possibility -- I can't say, but that order as I understand it forbids trade in other places," said Denis Zhuravlyov, executive director of brokers association NAUFOR, which runs the Russian Trading System (RTS).

"We've asked (the Federal Commission for the Securities Market) to explain whether trade in general is meant or just trade according to the principle...where trade is conducted without giving Gazprom (right of first refusal to buy shares)."
A government order last month gave approval to four regional stock exchanges to sell Gazprom shares from June 1, and retained the current rules for trade in Gazprom shares until July 1.
Trade in Gazprom shares in Russia is currently strictly controlled, with right of first refusal to buy any shares on offer reserved to the company itself.
A spokesman for the Securities Commission said on Friday that trade in Gazprom shares would cease on the RTS after July 1 if it was not included on the list of approved exchanges.

The government order did not rule out the possibility of buying Gazprom shares on the RTS, Zhuravlyov said, although he said he did not know how Gazprom shares could be bought on the exchange without being sold there.

He said the NAUFOR board of directors would meet soon to discuss the government order and its effect on RTS. He did not rule out the possibility RTS would apply to be included on the list of approved trading floors.
"The order talks about the sale (of Gazprom shares). Nothing is being said yet about buying, meaning theoretically, as I understand it, that you can sell there and buy wherever you want," he said.
